published_prior_art.cite: ArkhangelskyImbensLeiLuo2024, Theorem 4.1 leaves the time-varying dynamic DATE equation beyond scope; SunAbraham2021 studies conventional event-time regressors rather than reshaped finite-memory lags.
ArkhangelskyImbensLeiLuo2024, Theorem 4.1 already proves the homogeneous dynamic RIPW recovery; the explicit calendar-varying three-period separation is a useful strict-extension witness.
SunAbraham2021 supplies computable conventional event-study weight diagnostics, but no exact rational certificate for a reshaped finite-memory loading tensor.
Wright2026 and SunAbraham2021 give conventional-event-study contamination diagnostics, not an adjacent-mass necessary-and-sufficient sign/zero rule for reshaped carryover loadings.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4.1 assumes a finite-lag linear potential-outcome model with effects homogeneous over calendar time; the paper explicitly states that allowing time-varying dynamic effects makes the DATE equation more complicated and places its analysis beyond the paper's scope.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 225(2) (2021), primary article metadata/abstract; theorem text inaccessible; arXiv:1804.05785 consulted only as corroboration
source_verification_receipts.locator: Primary abstract; corroborating preprint Section 3, Proposition 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies absorbing-treatment event studies and shows that conventional dynamic FE lead and lag coefficients can load on treatment effects from other relative periods.

Under known sequential randomization, the paper defines lag-p dynamic causal effects and gives unbiased nonparametric estimators with finite-population limiting theory; it is an experimental-design result rather than an observational reshaped-FE loading theorem.
The manuscript identifies event-study effects in complex designs and then imposes a random-coefficients distributed-lag linear model whose effects remain constant over time.
The manuscript develops exact probability limits and computable contamination/negative-weight diagnostics for conventional staggered-adoption TWFE event studies, with orthogonal-score inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Systems Science and Information 11(5) (2023)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article proposes a time-varying-parameter distributed-lag model with coefficients conditional on past information; it is modeling precedent, not a causal panel reshaping result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Promote the ordered-sign handle first to a complete p=1 theorem over every positive absorbing support, including repeated adoption-time boundary cases, before attempting the arbitrary-p frontier.

Add a sample-level cross-fitted RIPW estimator and a consistency or asymptotic-normality result for the loading diagnostic, so the population tensor directly supports empirical use rather than only oracle interpretation.

Anchor the strict-extension comparison to the precise Section 4 equation and theorem of ArkhangelskyImbensLeiLuo2024 and explicitly state the inclusion of its homogeneous class in the calendar-varying class.

recommended_next_step: Advance this field-tier, well-posed novelty kernel to Stage 0, prioritizing the forward loading theorem and the p=1 ordered-sign base case.
